Metaplasia confined to uterine cervical epithelium, a reproductive site outside the axes.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; complete AV block and joint contracture each reported in 1/1 assessed patients. Small denominators limit frequency certainty.
Infectious abscess of the urethral glands; urethral disease belongs to the renal axis.
Excessive bacterial growth in the small intestine; classified as a digestive infectious disorder.
Tumour originates in the testis as a reproductive organ; endocrine dysfunction and qualifying distant organ involvement are not established.
Immune-mediated lichen planus with characteristic cutaneous blistering; common damaging oral involvement is not established for this variant.
Motor and developmental dysfunction results from fetal or infant brain injury; secondary orthopedic complications do not define the umbrella.
Aneurysm of an intracranial artery; location within the skull does not itself establish brain damage.
Congenital myopathy, developmental delay and cardiac septal defects define the syndrome; congenital strabismus is a defining ocular feature.
Dysplastic glandular neoplasm arising in the rectal mucosa.

GH/PRL-secreting pituitary tumour; GH-driven skeletal overgrowth and arthropathy reported in 80-99%. Diabetes and hypertension are separate diseases; skin thickening alone is insufficient.
Leiomyoma confined to the uterine corpus; uterine smooth muscle is reproductive tissue outside the musculoskeletal axis.
Carcinoma arising in a major salivary gland; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Genetic neurological disorder with epilepsy, intellectual disability and structural cerebral and cerebellar abnormalities.
Inflammatory joint disease; the umbrella includes degenerative and traumatic causes, so an infectious or immune mechanism is not universal.
Polycystic bone disease identifies a skeletal disorder; supplied information does not establish another affected organ.
Immune destruction of circulating platelets defines both the blood and immune axes; bleeding signs do not establish additional organ damage.
Acute cerebral dysfunction affecting attention, orientation and cognition; delirium is explicitly included in the neurologic axis.
Psychosexual desire disorder without an attributable physiological disease or demonstrated organ damage.
Infectious inflammation of the liver capsule associated with pelvic inflammatory disease; reproductive involvement has no axis.
Childhood renal cell carcinoma arising in the kidney; MiT translocations specify the tumour subtype.
